thesis: Even at the moment of public bara'ah, the passage commands believers to honor faithful treaty partners to term (9:4), confront hostility only within a revealed sequence with a binding release upon repentance (9:5), and grant individual asylum plus safe escort to any seeker who asks to hear the Qur'an (9:6).

flags.quote: But the passage itself refuses both distortions.
flags.issue: Check 4 on the sword verse: file presents the maximalist reading of 9:5 as mere 'shallow reading' while Ibn Kathir's own edition records it as a classical position (Ad-Dahhak: 'it abrogated every agreement of peace'; al-'Awfi's Ibn Abbas report). Al-Tabari records the ikhtilaf over whether 9:6 is abrogated (rules it is NOT — which supports the asylum thesis, but the file never mentions the dispute). Zero ikhtilaf acknowledgment, no tadabbur-vs-fatwa note, on the most contested fighting passage in the Quran, with a public 9:5 article depending on this reading.

flags.quote: In between stands the hard command for those who remain in declared hostility after the sacred interval passes.
flags.issue: Scope narrowing not carried by classical sources: file conditions 9:5 on active/declared hostility; al-Tabari defines targets by TREATY STATUS (no treaty / breakers / expired), and Ibn Kathir reads the command coercively. The hostile-only frame is an interpretive gloss presented as the verse's own logic without attribution.

flags.quote: Ibn Kathir's treatment of the passage keeps returning to that sequencing
flags.issue: Selectively true: Ibn Kathir does note grace period and release clause, but equally foregrounds sword-verse naming and abrogation reports. Overstates how irenic his emphasis is.

notes: Positive attributions all check out (Tabari's insalakha etymology verbatim; Tabari rules 9:6 not abrogated). Six cross-surah citations verified. Failure mode is one-sidedness, not fabrication: fix is additive — one honest paragraph on Dahhak/al-'Awfi vs Tabari-on-9:6, plus rewording 'declared hostility' to treaty-status language. IMPORTANT: the public 9:5 article rests on this file's reading — review it too.

thesis: Mockery of Allah, His signs, and His Messenger is not neutralized by the excuse 'we were only joking,' because jest can be the very form in which hidden disbelief enters speech.
notes: Tabuk sabab carried by all four editions (Ibn Umar camel report). No attributions to mismatch, no absolute claims, superlatives hedged. Takfir-adjacent but file stays contemplative, protects ordinary humor, applies as self-examination. Optional polish: one tadabbur/fatwa sentence on applying istihza'-kufr to modern speech.
